acceptance: Reproduce with SparkAdapter.create_connection() on local Spark 4.2.0 / JDK 17 and record the stack trace.

After the fix, create_connection succeeds repeatedly in one process, a TPC-H SF0.01 power run on local Spark completes, and the live Spark plan hook uses the adapter's connection instead of a private session.
A regression test covers the drop-then-reconnect sequence.
context:
Found during live plan parser validation (PR #3703). Not caused by that PR. Local only; no cloud.

Merged via PR #3977 as ce2b082c6. Root cause: existing-database handling validates through temporary connections; getOrCreate() returned the outer connection's session and close_connection() stopped it, so the drop step was skipped and CREATE DATABASE ran on a stopped session (null dagScheduler). Fix in benchbox/platforms/spark.py: a validation-time create_connection with a live session is a borrow, released not stopped on close. Live plan hook now uses adapter.create_connection(). Verified: 2 new unit tests fail before/pass after, repeated create_connection in one process, 4 live plan tests on Spark 4.2.0 local[1], TPC-H SF0.01 generate,load,power 22 queries with driver_memory=3g (default JVM exceeded the 8 GiB heavy-run limit). Unfixed follow-ups: SparkAdapter.test_connection() calls spark.stop() on a getOrCreate() session; two possibly flaky tests in tests/unit/test_heavy_choke_points.py on Python 3.14.
description: While capturing live Spark plans locally (Spark 4.2.0 local[1], JDK 17), SparkAdapter.create_connection() failed with a null DAGScheduler after its drop-database step, so the live plan hook had to build its own SparkSession. Reproduce through the adapter's own connection path, find whether the session is stopped/reused after the drop, and fix so the adapter can run local Spark benchmarks and the live plan hook can use the adapter connection again.
